summary: Édouard-Simon Ariel (1818–1854) was an Indology scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf from 1840 to 1844. He served as Conservator at the Bibliothèque publique de Pondichéry in 1846.
Élisée Reclus (1830–1905) studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban from 1848 to 1849. He later held a post at the New University of Brussels from around 1894 to 1905.

Émile Benveniste (1902–1976) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris and under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, Sylvain Lévi, and Louis Finot, later holding chairs at EPHE and Collège de France.

Linguist Émile Boisacq (1865–1945) studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Heidelberg University under Osthoff and Sütterlin, and the University of Paris under Bréal, Henry, and Meillet. He was professor of linguistics, Sanskrit, and Latin philology at Brussels (1895–1935).

Émile Bréhier (1876–1952) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris (~1897–1908) and under Henri Bergson. He later served on the faculty at the University of Paris from around 1919 to 1946.
Émile Chartier (1868–1951) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Pierre-Corneille (~1881–1886) and École Normale Supérieure (~1889–1892).

Émile Chatelain (1851–1933) worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1874–1880), he was affiliated with the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and held a post at EPHE from around 1881 to 1933.

Émile Durkheim (1858–1917) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at ENS, Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, and Bordeaux. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), EPHE (1905), and as professor at the Sorbonne (~1902–1917).
Émile Littré (1801–1881) was a scholar in linguistics and philosophy who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the Paris Medical Faculty (~1822–1830).

Émile Senart (1847–1928) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Munich under Martin Haug. He was a professor at the Collège de France and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

Émile-Louis Burnouf (1821–1907) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, University of Paris, and École française d'Athènes under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, he held posts at the University of Nancy and directed the Athens school (1867–1875).

Émilie Aussant works in Indology and linguistics, having studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. She was affiliated with Paris Diderot University (attested 2014) and became a university professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 2022.

Étienne Balazs (1905–1963) was a sinologist and historian who completed his doctoral studies under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later worked as a lead researcher at CNRS (1949) and professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

Étienne Lamotte (1903–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at KU Leuven, Rome under Carlo Formichi, Paris, and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, he taught at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and served as president at UCLouvain (1950–1959).

Étienne Marc Quatremère (1782–1857), a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and historical studies, studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held professorships at Rouen, Collège de France (Hebrew and Syriac, 1819–1857), and INALCO (Persian, 1827–1857).

Ñāṇamoli Thera (1905–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Exeter College, Oxford (~1924–1928). He later undertook traditional Buddhist training under Nyanatiloka Mahathera in 1949 and Palane Vajiranana in 1950.

Óscar Cortés is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied philosophy at the University of Guadalajara (2007–2013) and earned a master's degree at El Colegio de México (2015–2017). He was a researcher at Palabra de Clío (2018–2020).

Ösel Tendzin (1943–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu beginning in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

Ülo Valk (born 1962) is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He was educated at the Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1981–1986), where he held a post around 1995, and served as editor of Numen.

Čedomil Veljačić (1915–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Zagreb, where he became an assistant professor of Asian philosophy in 1961.
